verdict.rationale: Oneleet ships a first-party MCP server. Once a user connects an AI assistant through OAuth, the assistant "acts as you" and can see and do whatever the user's role allows, so the workspace can be driven with natural-language commands. Those commands go through an external assistant, not a native in-product interface, and the docs never list which operations the MCP tools expose. missing for 10: native in-product natural-language interface, documented list of MCP tools and actions covered, hands-on or independent corroboration of natural-language operation.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: add the Oneleet MCP server to your assistant, and it opens a browser window where you log in to Oneleet, review what the assistant is asking for, and pick the workspace it should work in.
Once connected, the assistant acts as you. It can only see and do what your own role in the workspace allows
You can connect an AI assistant to your Oneleet workspace by signing in with your Oneleet account.
